subject: The confession I wasn't going to send about your relationship
preview_text: One user went from 'this is stupid' to 'this saved us' in 30 days. Their secret is inside.
body_paragraphs: I almost deleted this email. Felt too personal. But then I remembered Sarah's message. She downloaded SoulPlan 30 days ago. Her first thought? 'Another gimmick. Our routine is fine.' Sound familiar?

Week 1: She begrudgingly added a 'Picnic at the new park' to the Shared Wishlist. Her partner saw it. Planned it as a Surprise Date for that Saturday. It wasn't about the picnic. It was that he noticed. Week 2: They used the AI to find a weird, budget-friendly pottery class. Laughed more than they had in months. By Day 30? Sarah told me, 'We're not just planning dates. We're remembering how to pay attention to each other.' The spark wasn't gone. It was just buried under 'What's for dinner?' and 'Did you pay the bill?'

The shift didn't happen with one grand gesture. It was the tiny, consistent nudge of the Shared Wishlist and Surprise Date Planner. He'd peek at her wishes. She'd plan a surprise from his. It became a silent conversation of 'I see you' instead of 'What should we do?' The app just held the space for that conversation to happen.

Your turn. Don't just browse ideas. Today, add one genuine, simple wish to your Shared Wishlist. 'Walk by the river at sunset.' 'Try that taco truck.' Then, send your partner a nudge. See what blooms. P.S. The couples who use the Wishlist feature just 3 times are 5x more likely to still be using the app in 60 days. It's the secret handshake.
